estimates.change: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls.
estimates.explanation: Have the remaining service generators (Frontier, and GCPUD if it is still covered) automatically metered or telemetered to BPA. BPA said it would set up the same kind of automatic recording for Grays Harbor. Bill Williams's instruction already treats automatic metering as the point where the hourly calls end. After the change the real-time traders stop the hourly generator and BPA calls and the initialling. They step in only when the meter feed fails. Grays Harbor is left out of the savings because BPA was already automating it and it stopped being a customer on Oct. 1.

stated_rate.words: at the top of EVERY hour

estimates.change: Warn the desk before month-end about deals ending at meters that still flow, and roll steady meters and tiny overflow volumes forward by rule instead of by email.
estimates.explanation: A list run before month-end matches meters with recent flow against Sitara deals that end that month, so Daren or the trader can extend or end each deal before the allocator finds the gap. Deals at meters that flow every month are entered as evergreen when the contract allows it, with the evergreen flag checked against the contract term at entry. Volumes under a small tolerance on days just past a deal's end attach to the prior deal by a rule the desk agrees in advance. Allocators then email Daren only about real renegotiations or contract questions, such as the Duke deal at meter 5892.

estimates.change: Produce a month-end file of each counterparty's official MTM by region, so Confirmations can answer period-end audit requests itself without asking the desks.
estimates.explanation: At each month-end, a scheduled job takes the official (officialized) month-end books and writes the total MTM for each counterparty short name, by region, without Delta/Vol, to a file Confirmations can open. When an auditor asks for a counterparty's value as of a month-end or year-end date, a Confirmations clerk looks the counterparty up and sends the figure. Desk heads and book admins no longer receive, forward, run, black out and export mini-books for these requests. Requests for other dates still go to a desk until the EnTelligence system Hunter is planning, with back-dated curves, is built.

estimates.change: Ask Credit to add the desk's rebook person to the Credit Report list so Giron no longer forwards it every day.
estimates.explanation: Credit adds Carole Frank (or whoever does the rebooks, or a desk group mailbox) to the Credit Report list. This is a one-time edit. Giron stays on the list. After that the report goes straight to the person who does the rebooks, there is nothing to forward each day, and rebooks are not held up while Giron is out.

estimates.change: Book deals with every ECC counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically and send a daily list of any that slip through, instead of a monthly search of all books.
estimates.explanation: EnronOnline would extend the rule it already has for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada to every counterparty that ECC has a master agreement with (Duke Energy Marketing, Aquila Canada and others), so those deals are booked to FT-US/CAND-ERMS from the start. A saved Tagg query, like the calculation Giron already uses to find these deals, would run each night and email Stacey Vallejo and the book's administrator any deal with ECC or a listed Canadian counterparty that sits outside FT-US/CAND-ERMS. The administrator moves it the next morning. At NYMEX close there is no request to everyone to search their books, and invoicing can start on time.

estimates.change: Turn on Access's automatic compaction for WeaponX so book admins no longer compact it by hand each week.
estimates.explanation: Whoever maintains WeaponX switches on the Access option that compacts the file automatically when it is closed (Tools/Options, 'Compact on Close', in Access 2000 and later), or adds a compact step at the end of the daily run. The fixed file goes out the same way a new copy was sent in Jan 2002, through a shared Dropbox folder. After that the file stays small without anyone acting, admins skip the shift-key open and the compact, and nobody has to send or forward reminders.

estimates.change: Have the weekly California Capacity Report built and emailed automatically from flow and price data, with the marketer only checking it.
estimates.explanation: Build a scheduled report that pulls Transwestern's California, San Juan lateral and East delivery volumes from Transwestern's own systems, El Paso's California delivery-point volumes from its posted operational data, and Gas Daily prices from the price feed. It works out the weekly averages, utilization percentages and price changes from the week before, fills in the existing template with the right week in the subject, and emails it to the same list every Friday. Michelle reviews it, adds a comment if needed, and no longer gathers and types the figures.

estimates.change: Have the mail administrators add the office and group to both address-book names so senders can tell the two Bills apart.
estimates.explanation: A mail administrator changes the two display names once, for example "Williams, Bill (Houston)" and "Williams III, Bill (Portland, ST West Hourly)", so the office shows when a sender types "Bill Williams" and picks a name. Senders choose the right person the first time, and neither Bill has to forward the mail or write a correction note.

estimates.change: Regular hours fill in automatically each pay period; staff record their own time off when they take it, so the email round and the 'I was here' replies stop.
estimates.explanation: Set the time system (or a shared team absence calendar that the assistant exports) to assume regular hours for every person each pay period. Staff enter vacation, sick or holiday days themselves when they take them, which takes about a minute. At the deadline Audrey Robertson runs the period report, checks it and submits it. She no longer sends a request, collects seven replies and types them in. People with no time off do nothing. A reminder goes only to people with a time-off entry that is not finished.

estimates.change: Book the GLO swap once as term deals with a zero-price GLO sale and formula-priced demand tickets, so the only monthly input is the crude value.
estimates.explanation: Risk/Logistics would book the HPL sale to GLO once for the whole term at zero price, keeping the volume. That removes the monthly zeroing and the risk of copying a priced ticket. The HPL-to-ENA and ENA-Wellhead demand tickets would also be booked once, with the demand amount set by formula as firm volume times the month's gas index, so the system calculates it when the index posts. The ENA-to-EGM demand ticket would be booked once for the term. Each month Settlements would enter the prior month's crude value on it in one place and check the result before flash.

stated_rate.words: This needs to be done monthly prior to flash

estimates.change: After each month-end, a scheduled job copies the existing P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for every gas book into one package for Arthur Andersen, so the monthly request, forward and gather cycle stops.
estimates.explanation: After each month's close, a scheduled job takes reports that already exist for every gas book: (a) the official P&L top page for the last business day, and (b) the top pages and curve-shift reports for the five days with the largest P&L (by size, gain or loss). It saves them in a read-only folder for AA. From March 2001 AA staff no longer had access to Enron Lotus Notes, so if AA cannot reach the folder, the same package is emailed to their Andersen address. A list showing which administrator owns which book sits beside it, and the controllers keep it up to date. AA picks the books it wants to test straight from the package and contacts the named administrator only to discuss what drove the P&L, which stays as it is today. Controllers no longer forward requests, administrators no longer pull and copy reports, and there are no second requests or 'who is responsible' questions.

stated_rate.words: As part of our monthly testing

estimates.change: Let settlements enter the invoiced monthly price on these deals once, when they validate the invoice, instead of emailing risk to change it.
estimates.explanation: For deals priced off the counterparty's monthly invoice, add a monthly actual-price field in Sitara (or a pricing formula that matches how the counterparty works out the price). The settlements analyst fills it in when validating the invoice, and risk sees the new price in the next P&L. No request email, no risk keying, no reminders, and no rerouting when risk staff change. Risk can still review the change in its normal P&L checks.

estimates.change: Build the roster each month from HR and phone-directory data instead of asking every assistant to check a spreadsheet.
estimates.explanation: A monthly report is pulled from the HR system (title, supervisor, location) and the phone directory (extension, fax) for the people in the EWS assistant pool, and sent to Ramirez. Assistants are no longer asked to check and reply. Wrong details are fixed in HR or the directory, which has to happen anyway when someone moves. Ramirez only reviews the generated file, and no mailing list has to be kept, so people wrongly on it are not bothered.

stated_rate.words: On a monthly basis I will be verifying information

estimates.change: Have the risk system email each book administrator and controller, every evening, the list of their post IDs not yet marked official, including flat ones.
estimates.explanation: IT would add a scheduled report to the risk system. It would hold each administrator's list of active post IDs and, at a set time each evening, email each administrator and their regional controller the ones not yet marked official, including those with zero position. It would resend until the list is empty. Administrators would no longer open the macro, type in the date and codes, and check the results. Controllers would get the same report instead of a separate verification sheet. Flat books would no longer slip through and end up on the list reviewed by Beck and Buy.

stated_rate.words: Let's make sure we are doing this every night.

estimates.change: Have the vendor send the report to a West Power distribution list (or auto-forward it by mail rule), so no one forwards it by hand.
estimates.explanation: Set up a distribution list (for example, DL-West Power Market Reports) with the 12 traders, and either change the vendor's delivery address to that list or add a mail rule in the assistant's mailbox that forwards the report to the list when it arrives. The trading desk owns who is on the list. Afterwards the report reaches the traders as soon as it arrives, with no daily step for the assistant, and adding a reader is a one-time list change.

estimates.change: Have a scheduled job compare the El Paso model with the CARP report each night, log the totals and a 'no variance' stamp itself, and flag only the variances for the trader.
estimates.explanation: Real Time Trading Support would set up a job or macro that runs after CARP finishes. It reads the day's El Paso model totals and the CARP report, compares them, and writes the totals and the result into the month's reconciliation file, creating the next month's file when needed. A timestamp shows Houston that CARP was run. If there is a variance, the job emails the shift a list of the hours and deals that differ, and the trader only has to write the explanation. On nights with no variance, nobody has to open the sheet, and a blank sheet can no longer be caused by a forgotten entry.

stated_rate.words: El Paso model must tie out with CARP when trading day is done.

estimates.change: Have Sitara roll each pipe's transport usage ticket into the next month automatically and fill its rate from the rate matrix, so staff key only the exceptions.
estimates.explanation: Sitara would be changed so a transport usage ticket can run open-ended by pipe and path instead of about three months at a time. Before each month it would add the new month and carry the prior month's volume forward as the starting estimate, instead of zero. The ticket's rate would be read from the maintained transport rate matrix instead of typed in. The person who sets up the tickets today (Heidi Withers in 2000) would then only enter exceptions: newly agreed baseload or third-party rates, and new tickets such as a new demand charge. Schedulers would update volumes as they learn them, but would no longer need to check every pipe for zeroed months. A monthly list of pipes with flow but no ticket would catch any that are still missing.

estimates.change: Send each month's curve questions straight to the trader who owns each curve, cc the desk head, and say up front what kind of explanation is needed.
estimates.explanation: Curve validation keeps a short list of which trader and desk head own each gas curve (taken from existing curve ownership) and sends each flagged curve's question straight to its owner, cc the desk head, instead of to Gossett or all three desk heads. The question says what counts as an answer (the specific market events behind the move, not only 'the market traded higher'), and notes when a curve is set equal to another one (for example NGI-PGE Topock equals NGI-SOCAL) so it only gets asked once. Afterwards the trader answers once, the desk head sees it in copy, and Jennifer gets one answer per curve without relays, chasers or a second round.

estimates.change: Run the report as a saved, scheduled query in the contract system and send it to a mail group readers join or leave themselves.
estimates.explanation: Set up a saved report in the contract system that lists all assignment, termination and expiration entries made since the last run, regardless of effective date. Schedule it to run before each bid week and send it to a mail group (or post it to a shared folder) that readers join or leave themselves. Cheryl stops building the report and editing the list. She only looks over each run before or after it goes out. Since the report runs on a schedule, it can no longer be forgotten.

estimates.change: Have the MIPS nightly file mark 'no data yet' as incomplete instead of zero, so POPS keeps Gas Control's estimate and schedulers stop overriding zeros by hand.
estimates.explanation: Measurement would have its MIPS vendor (SPI) change the nightly file so that a zero sent because no data has arrived is tagged incomplete. Gary Anderson in measurement named this as the only possible fix; SPI was looking into it, and the cost was not yet known and might need a work order. POPS would then keep Gas Control's estimate as the best available volume until a real measured volume arrives. Schedulers would no longer search for zeroed meters, retype estimates, re-allocate, or redo the work after a nightly roll. The P&L and UA4 would no longer be wrong during the month, and the escalation emails would stop.

stated_rate.words: tag all zero volumes sent in the nightly file process

estimates.change: Have the risk system save each region's liquidation detail to the shared FRED Liquidations year/month folder at month close, so it no longer has to be requested.
estimates.explanation: At month close a scheduled report writes each region's liquidation detail, split into the categories Jim already uses (price, basis, Gas Daily swaps, capacity hedges and so on), into ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations/<year>/<month>, the folder Jim already names. Jim opens the support himself and asks the desks only about items that do not tie out. Request emails, forwarding to analysts, hand-pulled deal lists and late catch-up requests go away.

estimates.change: Make the roll-off a scheduled setting in the risk calc, so one run produces both the 100% TDS view and the rolled V@R view.
estimates.explanation: Put the roll-off dates and percentages for basis and for Gas Daily and physical index into the calc as a calendar setting kept by the risk group. On roll-off nights a single calc writes the 100% prompt-month basis to the TDS post ID and the rolled-off basis to the Benchmark/V@R post ID, so administrators calculate and officialize once, as on any other night. A simple check lists any book whose Benchmark basis was not rolled, for Gossett or the regional lead to follow up. The monthly instruction email and the second calc, with its unofficialize and re-officialize steps, go away.

estimates.change: Have the system build and send the HL&P nominated-versus-actual month-to-date report every day, with short days flagged, instead of a scheduler updating and emailing a spreadsheet by hand each week.
estimates.explanation: Build a standard report from the nominations in Sitara/POPS and the meter actuals: nominated versus actual volume by day for the HL&P meters, month to date. It goes out every morning to the HL&P desk, volume management and logistics. It also flags days more than 5% below the nomination (the tolerance the desk quoted), so volume management sees the short days without waiting for logistics to list them. The scheduler only steps in where the meter data is missing or a nomination needs correcting. The desk still decides makeup and buybacks. Any shortfall figure has to use the pipeline's allocation between shippers, because the desk says that allocation decides how much shortage falls on ENA. The savings count only the weekly hand-built send, at the rate seen in Vaughn's 11 sends. The month-end question is not counted, since it shows up only once.

estimates.change: Set up each new ERMS curve in RisktRAC and TAGG automatically and report any gaps nightly, instead of request forms, emails and a weekly manual check.
estimates.explanation: Treat ERMS as the master list of curves. When a risk manager creates a curve in ERMS, a job creates the matching curve in RisktRAC and in TAGG, or puts it in a queue for RAR and the TAGG administrator to approve with one click. A nightly report lists any ERMS curve still missing from RisktRAC or TAGG. Afterwards the risk manager creates the curve once and sends no form or email; RAR and the TAGG administrator only handle the items on the exception report, and RAR no longer runs its weekly comparison by hand.

stated_rate.words: on a weekly basis new curves set up in ERMS are reviewed

estimates.change: Enter each origination grant once and have it post to both the granting book and the receiving book, so the receiving P&L cannot drift from the schedule.
estimates.explanation: The origination schedule becomes the only place a grant is entered (granting book, receiving origination group, deal, amount). That one entry posts the origination to the receiving book's P&L, so the book administrators stop keying it a second time. The analysts' nightly comparison then only has to catch the rare manual adjustment, and if one does turn up it goes straight to the book administrator named on the grant. Desk heads no longer relay these notices or search for who granted an amount.

estimates.change: Keep one shared Lotus Notes absence calendar that managers fill in once, so the vacation request-and-reply email round stops.
estimates.explanation: A shared Notes calendar or absence database is set up for the Energy Operations managers. Each manager enters planned vacation once, when it is approved, with the name of the person covering. Yvette and Brenda open the month's view instead of sending the request and merging replies. Colleagues can look up coverage in the same place, which can stand in for some of the separate vacation emails (those savings are not counted).

estimates.change: Send Settlements an automatic month-end list of new books and books that newly hold third-party financial deals, instead of a round of calls and emails to the risk leads.
estimates.explanation: Build a month-end report from the risk system's book and deal data (for example ERMS) that lists every book code created in the month and every book holding third-party financial deals in the invoice month that held none the month before. It is emailed to Settlements before the NYMEX invoice run. Settlements checks the list and contacts a risk lead only when an entry is unclear. The monthly call and email round and the contact list go away, and books are caught from the data rather than from someone remembering to report them.

stated_rate.words: invoices at the end of the month

estimates.change: Post the analyst charges as an automatic monthly allocation from the Org Database and send each charged manager the names being charged, instead of a hand-keyed entry that every manager must hunt for on the RC report.
estimates.explanation: Financial Operations sets the analyst charge up as a recurring allocation (or scheduled upload) that reads the analyst assignments per RC from the Org Database, which the mail already names as the source of headcount. Before it posts each month, the job emails each manager whose RC is being charged a short list of the analysts' names and the amount, with a few days to reply. Managers charged for no analyst do nothing. A manager who sees a name that has left replies, the Org Database is fixed, and the charge is right when it posts, so no correcting journal entry is needed. Financial Operations only reviews the allocation instead of building the file and keying the entry.

stated_rate.words: Financial Operations makes a manual Journal Entry each month to charge the appropriate RC.

estimates.change: Set up standing (evergreen) purchase and sale deals with El Paso at meter 986884 so each month's adjustment can be drafted without asking anyone for a deal.
estimates.explanation: Logistics and the trader (Daren Farmer) set up one evergreen purchase deal and one evergreen sale deal with El Paso, Teco's successor, at meter 986884. Both are priced the way the adjustment is settled today. Contracts, with George Weissman, would also write up the buy/sell arrangement, which runs for the remaining lease term, if they judge it safe to do so. In March 2000 Weissman was reluctant to raise it with Teco while other contracts were coming up for renewal, so the standing deals alone would still remove most of the chasing. Afterwards, Volume Management and Settlements allocate and draft each month's adjustment against the standing deal that matches its direction. They contact the trader only if a volume looks unusual or the counterparty changes again.

estimates.change: Replace the hand-built monthly buyback lists with a standing Sitara report of active industrial buyback and deficiency deals that anyone can run.
estimates.explanation: Buybacks are already entered in Sitara as deal tickets, and 601 points to the deal ticket as the place to record whether a buyback is still in effect. IT would set up a standing Sitara report listing active industrial buyback and deficiency deals by customer, meter and month, with their term and pricing. Julie, logistics (Robert Lloyd), Gas Control, the traders and settlements would run it instead of waiting for an emailed spreadsheet. Julie would keep the deal tickets current, as she must anyway, and check the report once a month rather than rebuild and send a spreadsheet; logistics would stop compiling its own copy of the list. Questions such as 'do we have an active buyback in place' would be answered from the report.

estimates.change: Let settlements enter the actual monthly demand charge on these transport deals themselves, so there is no email to risk and no wait before redrafting.
estimates.explanation: Give gas settlements rights to change the demand-charge field on pass-through transport deals such as #131389 and #131405 (or let Unify take the actual pipeline-statement amount directly). Settlements enters the amounts when it checks the pipeline statement, attaches its calculation as it does now, and redrafts Unify right away. Risk sees the change in its next P&L and can query it, but no longer keys it. This is the same kind of fix as the saved item for invoice-priced deals 27239 and 27253, but on different deals, a different field (transport demand charges, not commodity prices) and different requesters, so the savings do not overlap.

estimates.change: Fill the deal fields of each origination schedule entry from TAGG by deal number, and add Lagrasta's $0 deals automatically, so admins type only the origination value, group and originator.
estimates.explanation: Add a lookup to the origination schedule, either a spreadsheet macro or a TAGG extract keyed on deal number. When an admin enters a deal number, it fills in Book, Date, Customer, B/S, Term, Price and Pub code from TAGG. For Lagrasta's group, a daily extract of the group's TAGG deals adds any deal not yet on the schedule with $0 origination. Book administrators on the gas desks would use it. Afterwards they type the deal number, Origination Value, Origination Group and Originator, check the filled fields, and change the $0 on rows where origination is granted.

estimates.change: Give AA (or one Risk Controls contact for all desks) a read-only lookup by deal number that returns the deal ticket, confirmation and forwards detail, so the desk is asked only when a document is missing.
estimates.explanation: Build a read-only deal-document lookup: enter a deal number and get the deal ticket print, the executed confirmation and the forwards-detail report for that deal. Give access to the AA gas-testing team, or to one Risk Controls contact who serves AA for every desk. AA pulls the documents for the deals it samples each month. The desk head no longer reads and forwards the request, and the book administrator no longer gathers documents. The desk is asked only if the lookup is missing a document, for example a confirmation that has not been executed. Requests no longer stall while the desk head is away.
